rationale: Wheat is a primary gluten-containing grain per FDA (21 CFR 101.91). UNII: 79QS2MG2LP. Found on 1 product label in dataset.
Wheat is a primary gluten-containing grain per FDA (21 CFR 101.91). Not found as standalone excipient in US dataset but retained as catch-all. STARCH, WHEAT is the observed US variant.

FDA IIG lists 'wheat starch' as an inactive ingredient. Wheat is a primary gluten-containing grain per FDA (21 CFR 101.91). Not found in dataset under this exact string; US labels use 'STARCH, WHEAT' instead.
Rye is a primary gluten-containing grain per FDA (21 CFR 101.91). Not found in US dataset. No FDA IIG entry — extremely rare as pharmaceutical excipient.
Barley is a primary gluten-containing grain per FDA (21 CFR 101.91). Not found in US dataset. No FDA IIG entry — extremely rare as pharmaceutical excipient.
Semolina is coarsely ground durum wheat — contains gluten. Not found in US dataset. No FDA IIG entry.

Bran with no source specified — most common source is wheat. Flagged contains_gluten when source unspecified. Not found in US dataset under this exact string. NOTE: source-specified bran (e.g., RICE BRAN) is evaluated separately.

Malt is derived from barley via malting process. Barley is a primary gluten-containing grain. Not found in US dataset as standalone excipient. NOTE: maltodextrin, maltitol, ethyl maltol, and isomalt are chemically distinct compounds — NOT malt-derived — and are NOT in this table.

Pregelatinized starch with no source specified. Could be corn (gluten-free) or wheat (contains gluten). FDA IIG lists both source-specified and unspecified variants. Found on 8 product labels in dataset. No UNII code provided on those labels.

SSG Type A with no source specified. SSG = sodium salt of carboxymethyl ether of starch. Source could be potato (gluten-free) or wheat (contains gluten). UNII: 4ELV7Z65AP / H8AV0SQX4D. Found on 154 product labels. CRITICAL: NOT the same as croscarmellose sodium (which is cellulose-based).
SSG Type B with no source specified. Type B may have different degree of cross-linking than Type A. Source unspecified — could be wheat-derived. UNII: SP4S77AHO6. Found on 3 product labels.
EU naming for sodium starch glycolate. Same compound. Found on 1 product label under this exact string. UNII: H8AV0SQX4D (same as SSG Type A unspecified). Source unknown.

Produced by bacterial fermentation (Xanthomonas campestris). The National Celiac Association states xanthan gum does not contain gluten. While fermentation substrate can theoretically be wheat-derived, purification removes gluten proteins. Reclassified from 'unknown' to 'gluten_free' per National Celiac Association guidance. UNII: TTV12P4NEE. Found on 727 product labels. NOTE: Portuguese study flagged this precautionarily — our reclassification is a methodological departure documented in CLAUDE.md.

EU term for syrup derived from hydrolysis of starch. Source can be corn (gluten-free) or wheat (contains gluten). Not found in US dataset under this exact string — US labels use 'CORN SYRUP' or 'HIGH FRUCTOSE CORN SYRUP' when corn-derived.
FDA IIG term for glucose syrup. Source can be corn or wheat. Not found in US dataset under this exact string. When source is unspecified, gluten status unknown.
Starch that has undergone gelatinization with no source specified. Could be wheat-derived. Not found in US dataset under this exact string. US labels use PREGELATINIZED STARCH instead.

Chemically or physically modified starch with no source specified. Could be wheat-derived. Not found in US dataset under this exact string. US labels tend to specify source (e.g., MODIFIED CORN STARCH).
FDA CPG 578.100 term for modified food starch. Source unspecified. Not found in US dataset. Retained as catch-all.

Unqualified 'starch' with no source. FDA CPG 578.100 says unqualified 'starch' in the US legally = corn starch. However, a celiac patient reading the label cannot know this regulatory technicality. Flagged unknown for patient-facing analysis. Not found in US dataset under this bare string — US labels use 'STARCH, CORN' etc.

Naturally gluten-free but frequently cross-contaminated with wheat/barley/rye during growing and processing. FDA does not classify oats as a gluten-containing grain (21 CFR 101.91). Flagged unknown per precautionary approach. Not found in US dataset.
Derived from oats. Same cross-contamination concerns as oats. Not found in US dataset.
Corn is not a gluten-containing grain. Source explicitly specified on label. UNII: O8232NY3SJ. Found on 2,801 product labels — the most common starch excipient in our dataset.
Alternate naming for corn starch. Same substance as STARCH, CORN. UNII: O8232NY3SJ. Found on 1 product label under this exact string.
Latin botanical name for corn starch. Zea mays = corn. UNII: O8232NY3SJ. Found on 3 product labels.
Potato is not a cereal grain and contains no gluten. Source explicitly specified. UNII: 8I089SAH3T. Found on 33 product labels.
Alternate naming for potato starch. Same substance as STARCH, POTATO. Not found in dataset under this exact string.
Pregelatinized starch with corn source explicitly specified. UNII: O8232NY3SJ (same as corn starch). Found on 452 product labels.
Alternate naming for pregelatinized corn starch. Same substance. Not found in dataset under this exact string — labels use 'STARCH, PREGELATINIZED CORN'.
Another variant naming for pregelatinized corn starch. Found on 2 product labels.

Hydrolyzed starch product — corn-derived in the US. Despite 'malt' in the name, maltodextrin is NOT related to barley malt. It is produced by partial hydrolysis of corn starch. UNII: 7CVR7L4A2D. Found on 463 product labels.
Derived from cassava root. Not a cereal grain. Gluten-free. Not found in dataset.

Bran from rice. Rice is not a gluten-containing grain (21 CFR 101.91). Source explicitly specified — unlike unspecified 'bran' which defaults to contains_gluten. UNII: R60QEP13IC. Found on 2 product labels.

CRITICAL: Cellulose-based superdisintegrant (wood pulp/cotton). Sodium salt of cross-linked carboxymethyl CELLULOSE — NOT starch-derived. Often confused with sodium starch glycolate but is a completely different compound. Inherently gluten-free regardless of source.
Glucose syrup derived from corn starch hydrolysis. Corn is gluten-free. Source specified in name. UNII: 9G5L16BK6N. Found on 24 product labels.
Corn syrup enzymatically converted to increase fructose content. Corn-derived. Source specified in name. UNII: XY6UN3QB6S. Found on 377 product labels.
Dextrin ester with corn source specified. Corn is gluten-free. UNII: 89B2BSF9I3. Found on 1 product label. Note: incomplete parenthesis in original label data.
Gum arabic — exudate from Acacia senegal tree. Plant-derived gum with no cereal grain connection. UNII: 5C5403N26O. Found on 25 product labels.
Derived from guar bean (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba) — a legume. No cereal grain connection. UNII: E89I1637KE. Found on 31 product labels.
Produced by bacterial fermentation of Sphingomonas elodea. Unlike xanthan gum, gellan gum fermentation does not typically use wheat-derived substrates. UNII: 7593U09I4D. Found on 1 product label.
